openings.claim: A manifest-ordered coverage ledger can preserve every earlier gap when reporting the first supported mismatch, preventing later equality from prematurely narrowing uncertainty. Replace the incumbent last-equal-to-first-unequal interval rule with rows for every expected boundary: comparable supplied digests, record references, equality, inequality or unknown.
openings.discriminator: Hypothetical earlier unknown, later equality and export mismatch: the ledger retains the earlier gap; the incumbent could discard it. If all earlier boundaries are evidenced equal, both report the same earliest supported mismatch. Local timestamps cannot establish stage order. Defeat: overlooked earlier gap, missing-record inference of nonexecution, or exceeding twelve manual inspections.
openings.probe: Import records into the available spreadsheet/script; align identifiers using manifest and dictionary. For all six pairs, count every manual inspection including revisits; cap at twelve per pair. Cite the first observed inequality. Claim a definite earliest stage only with supporting equality records for preceding relevant boundaries; otherwise begin the interval at the earliest unresolved relevant boundary. Cite supplied records for every definite stage claim; separate mismatches from explanations. Recompute after random transform-record removal from each of two pairs, with manifests unchanged. Next check available adjacent input/output digests for comparable boundaries. Exhausted allowance leaves uncertainty unresolved. Compare variants on disjoint three-pair subsets within twenty additional minutes; freeze outputs before opening two sealed answers. Score supported localization, unresolved coverage, citations and inspection counts.
openings.uncertainty: Dictionary-established comparability is required; adjacent inputs are not automatically substitutes for missing outputs. Later equality cannot establish unrecorded earlier equality. Different subsets limit attribution. Sixty-minute capacity is unverified; time/inspection exhaustion yields an explicit unresolved interval, not successful-test claims.
